subject: literature
passage: My grandmother kept an album of pressed flowers that she had started as a girl. Each one lay flat between sheets of tissue paper, and over sixty years the bright petals had faded to shades of brown and gray, so that a rose and a poppy now looked almost the same. ______ when I turned the pages with her, she could name every flower and tell me the field, the garden, or the roadside where she had picked it.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

explanation.why: The second sentence says the flowers have faded so much that different kinds "looked almost the same." The last sentence says the grandmother could still identify every one. A transition that signals something true in spite of the previous point is needed.
explanation.A: Correct. "Nevertheless" shows that the grandmother could name every flower even though the faded petals all looked alike.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Naming each flower is not an example of the flowers fading; it goes against what the fading would lead you to expect.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "As a result" would mean the fading caused her to know each flower, but her knowledge exists despite the fading.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Likewise" signals a similar idea, but being able to name the flowers is unlike their having become hard to tell apart.
